subject: Output of categorical survey specific (obsCov) variables

messages.author: d00e519d6d1af813
messages.subject: Output of categorical survey specific (obsCov) variables
parts:
Hi all, 

I am running a single season single species occupancy model for an endemic chipmunk species. I have handful of categorical survey specific (obsCov) variables that I have hypothesized to influence detection probability. For example, the variable Summer torpor where the two states are Torpor (survey days in June) and Non-torpor (survey days not in June). When I run this categorical obsCov variable, I get the following output:

>   occu(~Torpor_summer ~1, data=occupancy.dataR)

Call:
occu(formula = ~Torpor_summer ~ 1, data = occupancy.dataR)

Occupancy:
 Estimate    SE     z P(>|z|)
   -0.658 0.202 -3.26 0.00113

Detection:
                                              Estimate   SE         z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)                                  -1.81 4843 -3.73e-04       1
Torpor_summerNon-torpor     -0.48 4843 -9.91e-05       1
Torpor_summerTorpor             -1.33 4843 -2.74e-04       1

AIC: 902.0803 

When I run categorical site specific (siteCov) variables, one of the states is the intercept (e.g., reference category). However, with obsCov variables, both states are visible. I am wondering if the results I am getting is what is meant to happen with categorical obsCov. 

When I set a reference category for this categorical obsCov variable, I get the following output: 

>   occupancy.dataR@obsCovs[["Torpor_summer"]] <- as.factor(occupancy.dataR@obsCovs[["Torpor_summer"]])
>   occupancy.dataR@obsCovs[["Torpor_summer"]] <- relevel(occupancy.dataR@obsCovs[["Torpor_summer"]], ref="Non-torpor")
>   occu(~Torpor_summer ~1, data=occupancy.dataR)

Call:
occu(formula = ~Torpor_summer ~ 1, data = occupancy.dataR)

Occupancy:
 Estimate SE  z P(>|z|)
   -0.658 NA NA      NA

Detection:
                                         Estimate SE  z P(>|z|)
(Intercept)                        -2.288 NA NA      NA
Torpor_summer                0.000 NA NA      NA
Torpor_summerTorpor   -0.848 NA NA      NA

AIC: 902.0803
Warning message:
Hessian is singular. Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates.

With this output the state "Non-torpor" is now the reference category (the intercept), but there are still two lines of data for the obsCov where one is zero. This makes me think that the output without the reference category is correct for categorical obsCov variables but wanted to make certain I am I am not missing anything.

Also, does the high SE values for the first example (no reference category) suggest that there is not enough data for this variable? The chipmunk has a relatively low detection probability (< 0.2). 

Thank you so much for your help in advance! Please let me know if I can provide any further information. 

Hailey

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Output of categorical survey specific (obsCov) variables
parts:
If you only have two possible levels of Torpor_summer, there should only be an intercept and one slope, not two slopes. Based on that output it looks like you actually have three levels of Torpor_summer, 'Torpor', 'Non-torpor', and ''.

Try running:

levels(occupancy.dataR@obsCovs$Torpor_summer)

and

unique(occupancy.dataR@obsCovs$Torpor_summer)

to confirm. Perhaps you have an empty string factor level where you meant to have an NA.

Ken
